label: LM Descent Stage Chassis

specs.material: Aluminum alloy 2219 with 25-layer Mylar/Kapton MLI blankets

function: Lower stage of the Apollo Lunar Module providing powered descent to the lunar surface, housing propellant tanks, the descent engine, landing gear, scientific equipment bays, and the ALSEP payload.
missionFacts: Performed the Powered Descent Initiation (PDI) burn at ~15,000 m altitude lasting 12 minutes to lunar surface
Housed four propellant tank pairs containing 8,165 kg of Aerozine-50/NTO hypergolic propellants
Served as the launch pad for the ascent stage after 21 hours 36 minutes on the lunar surface
Remains at Tranquility Base (0.67408° N, 23.47297° E) as humanity's first interplanetary monument

label: Ascent Stage Crew Cabin

specs.dimensions: 2.35 m wide × 3.76 m tall pressurized cabin

function: Pressurized crew compartment for two astronauts during lunar surface operations and ascent. Housed the Apollo Guidance Computer, Primary Navigation & Guidance System, forward egress hatch, docking tunnel, and RCS thrusters.
missionFacts: Armstrong and Aldrin had no seats — they stood for the entire 12-minute ascent, restrained by bungee cords
Ascent engine fired at 17:54:00 UTC on July 21, 1969 lifting off from the descent stage
Successfully docked with Command Module Columbia after 3 hours 41 minutes in lunar orbit
Jettisoned in lunar orbit; believed to have impacted the Moon within months of Apollo 11 mission

label: Cantilever Struts & Footpads

specs.dimensions: 9.45 m diagonal span across footpads, 0.94 m pad diameter
specs.material: Extruded 2024-T4 aluminum tubes with aluminum honeycomb crushable cartridges
specs.stroke: Up to 81 cm compression stroke per leg

function: Four folding landing gear assemblies that deployed during descent. Aluminum honeycomb cartridges stroked to absorb up to 1.5 m/s vertical touchdown velocity. Each forward leg carried a 1.73 m lunar contact probe.
missionFacts: "Contact light!" — Neil Armstrong reported the contact probe light at 20:17:40 UTC on July 20, 1969
Engine was shut down within 1 second of contact light to prevent hover plume from destabilizing the LM
Only 3 of 4 contact probes survived the landing intact; the fourth probe was bent on touchdown
The landing gear legs remain deployed at Tranquility Base, visible in Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter photographs

label: Descent Propulsion System (DPS)

specs.dimensions: 153 cm length, 148 cm bell diameter at exit

function: The first deep-throttleable rocket engine flown in crewed spaceflight. Gimbal-mounted ±6° for attitude control. Variable thrust from 10% to 100% allowed precise hovering and horizontal translation during landing approach.
missionFacts: Armstrong manually extended the hover phase by ~40 seconds to avoid West Crater boulder field
Engine shut down with approximately 25–30 seconds of usable propellant remaining in tanks
Throttle capability was essential: at 10% thrust the LM was near weightless over the final 30 m
Descent engine nozzle partially melts away during burn — normal for the ablative chamber design

label: S-Band Steerable High-Gain Antenna
function: Steerable parabolic dish transmitting live television, voice communications, biometric telemetry, and scientific data to NASA Deep Space Network stations across 384,400 km.
missionFacts: Transmitted the first live television from the lunar surface to an estimated 650 million viewers on July 20, 1969
Signal received simultaneously at Goldstone (California), Honeysuckle Creek (Australia), and Parkes Observatory
The 'Dish' at Parkes Observatory became primary receiver due to optimal geometry during moonwalk
Descended to lunar surface aboard Eagle's ascent stage separation; antenna remains on descent stage at Tranquility Base
